newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan cotton exports seen down on smaller crop.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan cotton exports seen down on smaller crop.

text.p: A forecast drop in Pakistani cotton production could cause exports to shrivel, cotton dealers said on Thursday.
"(Textile) spinners will make sure that no raw cotton, or very little, is exported this year," Nasim Usman, a dealer at the Karachi Cotton Exchange, said.

The state-run Pakistan Central Cotton Committee (PCCC) said on Tuesday that cotton output in fiscal 1996/97 (July-June) would be 9.2 to 9.5 million 375-lb bales, compared to last year's 9.96 million and a 1996/97 target of 10 million.
A PCCC statement blamed pests, leaf curl virus and weather factors for the reduced forecast.
"The next three to four weeks are crucial and could affect the yield per acre either way," the statement said.

Pakistani newspapers reported that the government was planning to impose a quarterly cap on cotton exports amid uncertainty over the crop size, but there was no official indication that the government was planning to dilute its free-trade policy.
